Yellow slide with a clay tablet covered in wedge marks and the Little Takhti character pointing. Text: 5-minute screen-free activity. Write like it's 5,000 years ago! Make a clay tablet with play dough and a pencil.

Green slide. You need: play dough, a pencil, 5 minutes. Step 1, make the tablet: roll a ball of dough and press it flat into a small rectangle. Step 2, make a reed pen: turn the pencil round, its flat end pressed in at a slant makes a wedge. Long ago, writers in Mesopotamia used a cut reed from the river as their pen.

Yellow slide. Step 3, press, don't drag: push the pen in and lift it out, each press leaves one little wedge. Step 4, write a message: a wedge for each person in your family, or a wedge code for your name. Wow fact: cuneiform means wedge-shaped; people in Mesopotamia, today's Iraq, wrote like this on wet clay about 5,000 years ago.

Green slide with the Little Takhti character cheering. Talk about it, then ask your little writer: Why was writing so useful to farmers long ago? What do we write on today, and with what? Can you find Iraq and its two rivers on a map? Free Mesopotamia worksheets and quiz, link in bio: littletakhti.com. Urdu tagline: Nanhe qadam, oonchi uraan.
